entry_documents.exposure: Treatment of a foreign passport bearing an amended gender marker at entry, visa issuance or airport processing is explicitly unsourced and unresolved; no domestic recognition framework exists for comparison.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch could feed into the unbounded morality provisions during any identity check.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Sections 353/354 ('good morals', public morality) are documented as used against people; de facto illegality of public same-sex conduct, no case law bounding scope, so prosecution exposure for an outed or visible visitor cannot be bounded. General context includes harsh prisons and suppression of opposition.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No express offence criminalising consensual conduct; no official violence cases cited in 2023.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any stop or complaint can route into the morality articles with unbounded reach.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation documented; absence flagged as a sourcing gap, not uniformity. Facility access rules for trans visitors not documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Country-wide morality provisions would apply wherever encountered.

care_services.exposure: No non-discrimination protection beyond employment; refusal of service, housing or facility entry on gender-identity grounds has no general legal remedy.
care_services.protection: Employment-field protection only; inapplicable to a visitor's care needs.
care_services.interaction: Care refusal interacts with a hostile social climate and absent recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Pervasive social and religious intolerance, status and conduct treated as taboo, no tolerated public discussion; authorities retain prosecution power under morality articles.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2023 report cites no cases of official violence; framing is societal, not state-directed.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Social hostility plus usable morality statutes raises both outing probability and post-outing severity.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans adult travelling with a minor would face the same taboo, family/community shunning dynamics and unbounded morality provisions; no custody- or family-specific rule documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor's presence could intensify community scrutiny in an intolerant social setting.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented societal pattern of discrimination; fear of shunning on disclosure. No trans-specific violence incident or prevalence figure exists in either direction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Complaints may be filed with police or the national human-rights commission; outcomes unrecorded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Thin documentation means absence of incidents evidences nothing about present street risk.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No general SOGI non-discrimination remedy; LGBTI organisations cannot register, so no domestic advocacy body; documentation scarce (2009–2012 baseline) and case law defining statutes absent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Police and human-rights commission complaints channel exists on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper channel with no recorded outcomes against a hostile social climate yields effectively thin recourse.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower: that anchor documents a routine police pattern of stops, confiscation and hours-long detention against trans visitors. This dossier documents no such pattern, no trans-specific incidents and no official violence, only usable morality statutes with unbounded scope.

Closest fit: a vague public-order/morality statute, routine unbounded exposure at identity checks, inconsistent and slow remedies, uncertainty about when checks become punishment. This dossier lacks that anchor's documented routine detentions and care denials, but adds a more intolerant society and thinner recourse.

Higher than this dossier: that anchor's harms stay administrative (secondary screening, refused admission, appeal desk with written reasons). Here unbounded morality prosecution plus no non-discrimination remedy and a taboo social climate make post-outing consequences materially worse.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime pairs de facto criminalisable public conduct (morality articles with no bounding case law) with zero general non-discrimination remedy, no LGBTI organisational infrastructure, and a society recorded as pervasively intolerant. Positives are thin but real: no express offence, no cited official violence, and a paper complaints channel. Crucially, the dossier flags its own silence — no incident data, no entry-document rules, no subnational detail — so absence of harm cannot be read as safety. Extrapolating from the structural signals (usable morality statute, no recognition, no recourse, hostile social climate, harsh general detention), an outed visitor faces unbounded prosecution exposure with effectively no remedy, placing the rating at the boundary of High/Elevated risk, not above it.
